subject: Request: Vaulted/private deployment operational scenarios and operator Q&A
messages:
From: Alice Tran <alice.tran@helixhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@helixhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Vaulted deployment operational scenarios & operator questionnaire

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Helix is compiling a short procurement packet for our regulated edge sites and we need more granularity on how Redwood would operate in a vaulted (air-gapped / no egress) deployment. The attached PDF is our questionnaire (Helix_RFI_v1.pdf) — a mix of specific operational scenarios and evidence requests.

Top items we care about right now:
- Operator access model: how do operators connect (if at all) for emergency fixes?
- Patch and rollback windows: how are OS and runtime patches staged and applied in an offline environment?
- Key management: support for HSM/KMS and operator access constraints.
- Telemetry/traceability: what local telemetry is kept, retention, and how do we attest to no egress?

Can you send a draft response by EOD Friday? Also let us know if you want a short call to walk through the questionnaire.

Appreciate it — Alice

[Attachment: Helix_RFI_v1.pdf (149KB)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alice Tran <alice.tran@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Vaulted deployment operational scenarios & operator questionnaire

Hi Alice —

Thanks for sending the questionnaire. We've started a draft and attached an initial answers doc (Vaulted_Deployment_Answers_v0.3.docx). High-level notes:

- Operator access: Redwood supports a locked operator model for vaulted installs. Operators never get outbound access from the runtime. Emergency operator actions are performed via a controlled console that is enabled by customer-administered one-time tokens. We describe the token issuance flow and the audit trail in section 2.1 of the attached.

- Patching & rollback: We support staged patch bundles delivered via signed import packages (airgap bundle). The operator imports bundles into a staging partition; packages are validated via signatures and checksum before activation. We include an offline rollback mechanism that preserves KV cache and model artifacts for fast rollback. See section 3.2.

- KMS/HSM: We support external HSMs (PKCS#11) and customer-managed KMS. Keys used by the runtime are wrapped and never leave the hardware boundary. Operator access to key material is limited to wrapped key import requests, which must be approved by an on-prem admin.

- Telemetry: Local telemetry is retained in encrypted local storage. For customers who require absolute no-egress, we provide a local-only telemetry store and a signed audit manifest export that can be handed to auditors.

We're happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through specifics. Irene and Karthik are on this thread; Karthik has a sample operator-runbook and I'll attach that next with examples.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Vaulted_Deployment_Answers_v0.3.docx]

From: Alice Tran <alice.tran@helixhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@helixhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@helixhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Vaulted deployment operational scenarios & operator questionnaire

Vivek —

Thanks for the quick draft. A few clarifying questions from Security:

1) Token issuance: can tokens be scoped to single-command sessions (timebound + action-bounded) and are they revocable after use? We need a description for our SOPs.

2) For the airgap bundle: what signing algorithm and key lengths do you use, and can we require that bundles be signed with our HSM-backed key?

3) Runbook example: can you include a typical emergency operator workflow that shows the exact commands and the audit log entries produced? That helps our compliance reviewers.

Also, procurement asks whether Redwood will accept a staged SaaS fallback for noncritical workloads during onboarding (i.e., temporarily enabling outbound connectivity under a formal change window). Please include the commercial constraints in the next draft if this is possible.

We can take a 30-min call on Monday; are you available?

Regards,
Alice

[Helix: note — procurement is asking about fallback; security is focused on single-use tokens and HSM signed bundles.]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: Vaulted deployment operational scenarios & operator questionnaire

Vivek / Irene — forwarding Alice's clarifications and adding internal notes for the next draft.

Internal action items (short):
- Expand token model: add single-command, timebound token flow + revocation API and example JWT payload. Provide example audit log lines (timestamp, actor, action, token_id, result).
- Airgap bundle signing: confirm support for RSA-4096 or ECDSA-P384 per Helix request; confirm ability to ingest customer-signed bundles issued by their HSM — engineering OK.
- Runbook: attach operator-runbook-example.md with a redacted CLI session and sample log entries.
- Commercial: note around staged SaaS fallback = possible, requires signed change window, written SLA amendment and temporary networking controls; finance to confirm credit/discount terms.

I'll prep an updated answers doc (v0.4) with the above included and a short appendix with example audit manifests. Vivek — can you handle the commercial blurb to confirm what we can offer for a staged fallback? Irene — can you pull the runbook example and scrub customer-facing IDs?

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Deployability
Redwood Inference
